Hi Eva — great question. Short version up front: we bill above-commit usage on a per-GPU-hour basis with a stepped overage multiplier and provide configurable throttling policies plus an optional burst add-on. Details below.

Billing (above-commit):
- Metering: GPU consumption is metered per-minute and aggregated into GPU-hours with 1-minute granularity. We also account for concurrent multi-GPU jobs as summed GPU-seconds.
- Rates: baseline committed rate (R) applies to the committed GPU-hours. Above-commit usage is billed at a multiplier of R: 1.2x for the first 30 days of sustained overage, then 1.5x thereafter, unless a negotiated cap is in place.
- Tiered discounts apply to committed volume only (see attached pricing workbook).

Operational handling:
- Soft throttling: for transient spikes (< 6 hours), we allow requests to complete and surface higher latency. No throttling by default.
- Sustained overage (> 48 continuous hours or > 120% of commit for 3 days): we will trigger the customer-configured policy: (a) AUTO-BURST if enabled (automatic temporary allocation from our spare pool, billed at 2.0x rate), (b) QUEUE (requests are queued up to a configurable backlog depth), or (c) HARD-THROTTLE (reject new requests with 429s for non-priority routes).
- Priority tiers: we support route-level priority. Critical routes can be pinned to not be throttled (subject to capacity availability and higher overage pricing).

Transparency & tooling:
- All overage metering and throttle events are visible in the Console (per-minute charts, alerts).
- Audit logs and per-request traces are exposed for billing reconciliation.

Attachments: I attached the latest pricing workbook and a short SLA summary.

If you want, Priyom can propose a commit/discount structure and Monica can map the technical throttle behavior to your routes.

Best,

Eva — quick technical clarifications to help procurement:
- Metering specifics: we report both GPU-hours and per-token billing for mixed workloads; the Console shows a breakdown by model, route, and GPU utilization.
- Throttle behavior: when QUEUE is active, requests remain in pre-execution state for up to 120s before being executed; beyond that we return a 202 with a job id for async retrieval. This is configurable per-route.
- Failover: you can optionally enable automatic fallback to Hosted API for non-sensitive requests — that path has separate pricing and is subject to regional availability.
- Audit evidence: we can include a usage export CSV for your procurement audit (per-minute, per-route for last 12 months).

If procurement wants firm worst-case numbers, Priyom and I recommend Option B with the 90-day overage grace and a capped 1.3x multiplier for the first billing cycle. That gives predictable economics while preserving flexibility.
